scope: Independent bounded source, current Mach-O symbol/export/disassembly, and saved runtime-image review. No source edits, build, fetch, target access, or hardware execution. This report is the only file written.

conclusion.confirmed_defect: The booted libSystem.B exports its own initialized 4096 vm_page_size, while its mach_init call resolves to libdyld, which initializes a different vm_page_size alongside the canonical masks and shifts. The exported size and the initialized size are different storage objects.
conclusion.minimal_patch: Delete exactly vm_size_t vm_page_size = 4096; at src/Libraries/libSystem/stub/pd_libSystem_compat.c:711. Preserve libSystem.exports:298 and the existing -reexport_library libdyld link at stub/CMakeLists.txt:324-327.
conclusion.source_api: Keep the public data ABI: extern vm_size_t vm_page_size in mach/vm_page_size.h:42. No new getter, local cache, initializer assignment, commpage reader, or hardcoded page size is needed. A declaration without an initializer that is still a definition is not a forwarding fix.
conclusion.required_correction_to_grok_report: The link_note/why_this_is_enough claim that -u,_vm_page_size should pull mach_init.o into libSystem is not the desired mechanism and is not established by this binary. Current libSystem has no defined mach_init; it imports that function from libdyld. The correct rebuilt result is canonical data forwarding to libdyld, matching the existing kernel-size/kernel-mask exports. Reject a new local uninitialized or initialized duplicate even if linking succeeds.
conclusion.approval_limit: The proposed one-line deletion is justified because the forwarding dependency and exported canonical target already exist. This review did not inspect a completed patched dylib or execute it. Root must establish the linked result before staging.

runtime_binding.method: Independently hashed the full image and saved raw console. Used debugfs -R cat (read-only; no -w, mount, or extracted-file writes) to hash the three image members below; both dylibs equal the current jll store bytes. Parsed/compared the report values against the raw JSON console line.
runtime_binding.protection_results: Saved probe succeeds for aligned mprotect, rejects +4096 and +8192 with EINVAL, and succeeds for all three vm_protect calls; this is real saved runtime evidence, not a current execution.

binary_findings.evidence: arm64-apple-darwin20.4-nm -m; llvm-objdump --macho --exports-trie; independent LC_SEGMENT_64 file-offset decoding
binary_findings.libSystem: _vm_page_size is external __DATA,__data at unslid 0x2b6800; file bytes decode as uint64 4096. _mach_init, _vm_page_mask and _vm_page_shift are undefined from libdyld. _vm_kernel_page_size and mask are explicit re-exports. No local mach_init definition is present.

binary_findings.meaning: All six globals are external definitions in __DATA,__common and in the export trie. Their zero-fill on disk is intentional; mach_init initializes these same addresses.

binary_findings.evidence: Mach-O load commands, not otool -L alone
binary_findings.dependency: libSystem has LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB (0x8000001f) /usr/lib/system/libdyld.dylib. libdyld has ordinary LC_LOAD_DYLIB /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib. The libSystem ID is not an extra dependency. The whole-library re-export also exposes mask/shift even though libSystem.exports omits their explicit names.

binary_findings.stores: mach_init_doit 0x5ed90-0x5edcc reads USER_PAGE_SHIFT_64 at 0xfffff4025, stores shift to its own 0x993e8, stores 1<<shift at its own 0x993d8 (instruction 0x5edbc), then reloads that same size at 0x5edc0 and stores size-1 to 0x993e0. Kernel trio uses commpage 0xfffff4037 and addresses 0x993c0/0x993c8/0x993d0.
binary_findings.correction: In this actual build the mask path reloads the libdyld-local size; no optimizer/register-retention hypothesis is needed to explain the mismatch.

binary_findings.initialization_order: pd_libSystem_initializer at 0x9cf7c calls its own __libkernel_init at 0x9d0c8. That wrapper calls import stub 0x26c6f4 for libdyld mach_init at 0xbadd4. Then initializer calls the explicit libdyld wrapper at 0x9d0dc via stub 0x26c7c0; __malloc_init follows at 0x9d160. libdyld pd_libdyld_libkernel_init 0x5d680 calls its own __libkernel_init 0x5f090. mach_init has an idempotence flag, not a late constructor that runs after malloc.

source_evidence.finding: Strong initialized local compatibility definition is the incorrect exported size.

Export names become -u roots and the export list; libdyld is linked and whole-library re-exported. Preserve these; -u is an unresolved-symbol requirement, not proof of which archive object will be selected.
libdyld links libsystem_kernel_static; its unexport list hides C++ internals, not the Mach page globals.
Both libkernel tables initialized before malloc. Their hidden table duplication does not require public page-global duplication.
Explicit wrapper enters libdyld-local kernel initializer.
Canonical globals; commpage-derived shift/size/mask; idempotent call. No source change needed.
Public extern variable ABI; round_page uses size, mach_vm_round_page uses mask, so split storage matters.
User allocation quantum follows vm_page_size; guard quantum is max of kernel and user sizes.

Postlude guard starts at user round_page_quanta and uses large_vm_page_quanta_size; observed 4K start/16K task alignment mismatch explains the warning mechanism. Do not change protections or suppress warnings.

ordered_validation_for_root: Build the isolated one-line deletion using the existing pinned recipe. No extra local definition or initialization function; leave allocator/kernel/commpage code intact.

Inspect rebuilt libSystem nm plus export trie/chained imports: no N_SECT/N_ABS/common _vm_page_size definition, canonical re-export to libdyld, and no newly selected local mach_init. Inspect libdyld still exports all six globals and its mach_init stores into its own exported tuple. If linker selection differs, stop and fix forwarding rather than adding a local copy.

Bind the rebuilt dylib bytes in the staged RAM image; retain the unchanged page-probe binary. Check getpagesize, host_page_size, vm_page_size, mask=size-1 and 1<<shift=size agree on this actual 16K guest. Misaligned mprotect must still fail; no permission relaxation. Re-run the previously warning-producing program in a separately authorized cycle and preserve any remaining warning.
Treat compile/link/export success as artifact evidence only. A later target run must validate page values and allocator behavior; this review authorizes no hardware action.
